questions.question: Which device integrates a CPU, memory, and I/O peripherals on a single chip?
questions.explanation: A microcontroller integrates the processor core, memory (RAM and flash), and peripherals such as timers and GPIO on one chip, unlike a microprocessor which requires external components.

questions.question: What does RTOS stand for?
questions.explanation: RTOS stands for Real-Time Operating System, designed to process data and respond to events within guaranteed time constraints.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of a real-time operating system?
questions.explanation: An RTOS is defined by determinism — it guarantees that critical tasks respond within bounded, predictable time limits rather than maximizing average throughput.

questions.question: What is an interrupt in an embedded system?
options: A signal that suspends normal execution to handle an urgent event
A fault that permanently stops the processor
questions.explanation: An interrupt is a hardware or software signal that pauses the main program so the CPU can execute an Interrupt Service Routine to handle a time-critical event.

questions.question: What does GPIO stand for?
questions.explanation: GPIO stands for General Purpose Input/Output — pins whose behavior (input or output) is configured by software and used to interface with external devices.

questions.question: Which serial protocol communicates over the SDA and SCL lines?
questions.explanation: I2C uses two wires: SDA (Serial Data) for data transfer and SCL (Serial Clock) for synchronization, allowing multiple addressed devices on one bus.

questions.question: In SPI communication, which line selects the slave device to talk to?
questions.explanation: The Chip Select (also called Slave Select) line is pulled active by the master to choose which slave device participates in the SPI transaction.

questions.question: Which serial protocol transfers data asynchronously on TX and RX lines without a shared clock?
questions.explanation: UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) sends data over TX/RX lines without a clock line; both ends must agree on the baud rate beforehand.

questions.question: What is firmware?
options: Software stored in non-volatile memory that provides low-level control
questions.explanation: Firmware is software permanently stored in a device's non-volatile memory (like flash or ROM) that controls the hardware at a low level.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a watchdog timer?
options: Track the current time of day
Reset the system if software fails to respond in time
questions.explanation: A watchdog timer must be periodically refreshed ('kicked') by software; if the program hangs and fails to do so, the watchdog resets the system to recover.

questions.question: Which platform is a popular open-source microcontroller board for prototyping?
questions.explanation: Arduino is an open-source electronics platform built around simple microcontrollers (like the ATmega328P), widely used for rapid prototyping and education.

questions.question: Which device is a single-board computer that typically runs a full Linux operating system?
questions.explanation: The Raspberry Pi is a single-board computer with a microprocessor capable of running a full OS like Linux, unlike microcontroller boards which run bare-metal code or an RTOS.

questions.question: What does a sensor do in an embedded system?
options: Converts electrical signals into physical motion
Converts a physical quantity into an electrical signal
questions.explanation: A sensor measures a physical quantity (temperature, light, pressure, motion) and converts it into an electrical signal the system can process.

questions.question: What does an actuator do?
options: Converts an electrical signal into physical action
questions.explanation: An actuator converts electrical control signals into physical action — examples include motors, solenoids, relays, and LEDs.

questions.question: Which technique do embedded devices use to save power when idle?
questions.explanation: Embedded devices conserve energy by entering sleep or low-power modes that halt the CPU and disable unused peripherals until an event wakes them.

questions.question: What type of real-time system treats a missed deadline as a complete system failure?
questions.explanation: In hard real-time systems (pacemakers, airbags), missing a deadline is catastrophic and counted as total failure; soft real-time systems tolerate occasional misses.

questions.question: What is the code executed in response to an interrupt called?
questions.explanation: The Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) is the function the CPU jumps to when an interrupt fires; it should be short and fast to minimize disruption.

questions.question: Why can multiple slave devices share a single I2C bus?
options: Each device has a unique address
Each device uses a separate clock
I2C uses dedicated wiring per device
questions.explanation: Every I2C device is assigned a unique 7-bit (or 10-bit) address, so the master can select which device it is communicating with over the same two wires.

questions.question: Compared to I2C, what advantage does SPI typically offer?
questions.explanation: SPI supports full-duplex communication (MOSI and MISO simultaneously) at higher clock speeds than I2C, at the cost of more wires and a select line per slave.

questions.question: What does baud rate specify in UART communication?
options: Number of symbols transmitted per second
The size of the transmit buffer
questions.explanation: Baud rate is the number of signal symbols (effectively bits, in standard UART) transmitted per second; both devices must be configured to the same rate.

questions.question: Which type of memory loses its contents when power is removed?
questions.explanation: SRAM is volatile memory used for variables and the stack during execution; flash, EEPROM, and ROM are non-volatile and retain data without power.

questions.question: Where is application firmware typically stored on a microcontroller?
questions.explanation: Firmware is stored in on-chip flash memory, which is non-volatile, so the program persists across power cycles and can be reprogrammed.

questions.question: What does an Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) do?
options: Converts digital values into analog voltages
Converts an analog voltage into a digital number
questions.explanation: An ADC samples a continuous analog voltage (like a sensor output) and produces a discrete digital value with a resolution determined by its bit width.

questions.question: What does Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) control by varying a signal's duty cycle?
options: The frequency of the CPU clock
The baud rate of serial data
The address of a slave device
The average power delivered to a load
questions.explanation: PWM switches a digital pin on and off rapidly; varying the duty cycle changes the effective average voltage, controlling LED brightness or motor speed.

questions.question: What is 'debouncing' in embedded systems?
options: Filtering spurious transitions from mechanical switch inputs
Reducing clock speed to save power
questions.explanation: Mechanical switches physically bounce, producing rapid false transitions; debouncing (in hardware or software) filters these so one press registers once.

questions.question: What is a cross-compiler used for in embedded development?
options: Compiling code on one platform to run on a different target platform
questions.explanation: A cross-compiler runs on a development machine (e.g., a PC) but produces machine code for a different target architecture, such as an ARM microcontroller.

questions.question: A microcontroller outputs a PWM signal at 25% duty cycle with a 3.3 V logic-high level. What is the average output voltage?
questions.explanation: Average voltage = duty cycle x Vhigh = 0.25 x 3.3 V = 0.825 V.

questions.question: Which on-chip peripheral allows an MCU to read an analog temperature sensor's voltage?
questions.explanation: An analog-to-digital converter samples the analog voltage and produces a digital value the firmware can read.

questions.question: An embedded system reboots automatically whenever firmware hangs because a dedicated timer is no longer being refreshed. What provides this behavior?
questions.explanation: A watchdog must be periodically 'kicked' by healthy firmware; on expiry it resets the system to recover from hangs.

questions.question: Which serial bus connects multiple addressed peripherals using just two shared lines, SDA and SCL?
questions.explanation: I2C is a two-wire (data + clock) multi-device bus using 7-bit addressing; SPI needs separate chip-select lines.

questions.question: Which RTOS mechanism mitigates priority inversion when a low-priority task holds a mutex needed by a high-priority task?
questions.explanation: Priority inheritance temporarily boosts the mutex holder to the waiting task's priority so it finishes and releases the lock quickly.
